research_method_note: Research done on 2026-10-09 with WebSearch only (24 queries). WebFetch and direct HTTP access were unavailable (DNS/proxy errors), so no article was read in full: every fact below comes from search-engine summaries of the cited pages. Source numbers [n] match section 13 of investigacion.md. Items marked SNIPPET-ONLY or DISPUTED must be checked against the full article before publishing.

video_metadata.working_title: HAWAII 1991 Cold Case Solved After 32 Years — Justice for Dana Ireland
video_metadata.topic_one_sentence: On Christmas Eve 1991, 23-year-old Dana Ireland was struck while riding a bicycle in Kapoho, Puna, abducted, sexually assaulted, beaten and left on a fishing trail; three Native Hawaiian men were convicted, two were later exonerated and the third died in prison, and in 2024 genetic genealogy led police to Albert Lauro Jr., who died by suicide before any charge.
video_metadata.primary_emotion_to_evoke: grief turning into outrage at a system that convicted the wrong men, then bittersweet relief at the truth arriving too late for a courtroom

protagonist._instructions: Main character: the victim, Dana Ireland (the story is victim-centred). The man identified by DNA is described in supporting_characters.
protagonist.age_at_time_of_events: 23 (born December 12, 1968 according to Find a Grave / WikiTree; SNIPPET-ONLY, genealogy sites)
protagonist.occupation_or_status: Recent graduate of George Mason University (1991); hoped to work in the physical therapy field [29][33]
protagonist.location: Visiting her family in the Kapoho area of Puna, Hawaii Island (Big Island), from Virginia [3][29]
protagonist.physical_description: Not used (no verified description beyond photos).
protagonist.background_brief: Born at Fort Belvoir, Virginia (genealogy sites) and raised in Springfield, Virginia, a suburb about 11 miles southwest of Washington, D.C. [28]. Daughter of John Ireland, a retired Army officer, and Louise Ireland [29][32]. Her older sister Sandra (Sandy) had moved to Hawaii when Dana was little; one account says Sandy moved to the Kapoho area in 1977 [29].
protagonist.psychological_profile: Family and friends recalled her as shy, kind, loyal, an athlete, a sweet daughter and a tomboy (Star-Bulletin feature by Cynthia Oi, June 8, 1999) [28].
protagonist.mundane_humanizing_detail: On the afternoon of December 24, 1991 she wanted to invite a friend to the family's Christmas party the next day; offered the family car, she preferred to ride a bicycle for the exercise (secondary account, SNIPPET-ONLY) [51][63]. Another account says she was riding to the family's rented vacation home [33].

individuals.name: Dana Ireland
individuals.specific_impact_suffered: Struck by a vehicle while cycling on Kapoho Kai Drive, abducted, sexually assaulted, beaten and left on a fishing trail off Waa Waa Road; died at Hilo hospital just after midnight on December 25, 1991, from her injuries and massive blood loss [3][13][29][33]
individuals.humanizing_detail: shy, kind, loyal, an athlete, a tomboy [28]

individuals.name: Albert "Ian" Schweitzer
individuals.role_or_profession: Native Hawaiian man from Puna; about 20 in 1991 (derived from age 51 at release in 2023 [33])
individuals.connection_to_protagonist: Wrongfully convicted (verdict February 16, 2000) of second-degree murder, kidnapping and first-degree sexual assault; life plus two consecutive 20-year terms, reported as 130 years [14][20]
individuals.specific_impact_suffered: Conviction vacated and charges dismissed January 24, 2023 by Judge Peter Kubota; released the same day after more than two decades in custody (reports range from 23 to 26 years) [14][15][17][19]
individuals.humanizing_detail: Appeared at a news conference with his mother and relatives after release [18]
individuals.any_quotes_from_them: "I'm just grateful, very thankful." (January 2023) [18]; his feelings were "all over the place. Nerves, anxiety, scared." [18]; "My family and the Ireland family are all victims of this terrible injustice." (January 2025 statement) [35]

individuals.name: Shawn Schweitzer
individuals.role_or_profession: Ian's younger brother; reported as 16 at the time of the crime [MINOR in 1991] [14][34]
individuals.connection_to_protagonist: Pleaded guilty in 2000 to manslaughter and kidnapping in a deal requiring him to implicate his brother and Pauline; credit for about one year served plus five years' probation [13][14]
individuals.specific_impact_suffered: Recanted (October 2022, per Innocence Project summary); conviction vacated and case dismissed October 23, 2023 [16][21][22]
individuals.humanizing_detail: Said he pleaded guilty because his parents did not want to risk losing another son [21][22]

individuals.name: Frank Pauline Jr.
individuals.connection_to_protagonist: Gave police statements in 1994 while in custody on unrelated charges, implicating himself and the Schweitzers; later said he did it to help his half-brother with drug charges; recanted in 1996 [26][27]
individuals.specific_impact_suffered: Convicted 1999; conviction upheld by Hawaii Supreme Court 2002; sentence reported differently (180 years, 160 years, consecutive life terms) DISPUTED [20][27][55]. Killed April 27, 2015, aged 42, at Southern New Mexico Correctional Facility, Las Cruces [24][25]. Posthumous petition to vacate his conviction was pending/delayed as of January 2024; no later ruling found [23]
individuals.humanizing_detail: Transferred from Hawaii to the New Mexico prison in December 2012 [24]

individuals.name: John Ireland
individuals.specific_impact_suffered: Spent the rest of his life campaigning for crime victims; helped pass Hawaii laws letting families speak at sentencing and allowing life without parole for especially 'heinous, atrocious, or cruel' murders (not retroactive); died in Virginia around October 31, 2000, aged 76 [32]
individuals.humanizing_detail: With Louise, moved to Puna for some months in 1994 to press for an arrest; returned in 1996 with a petition of several thousand signatures [33]

individuals.name: Louise Ireland
individuals.specific_impact_suffered: Died in 2016 at 92 (Find a Grave / WikiTree, SNIPPET-ONLY) [53]

individuals.name: Sandra (Sandy) Ireland
individuals.specific_impact_suffered: Among the first to arrive where Dana's bicycle wreckage was found; testified at Pauline's 1999 trial about the last time she saw Dana [30][31]
individuals.humanizing_detail: Moved to Hawaii when Dana was little [29]

collective_victims_if_applicable.group_description: The Ireland family; the Schweitzer and Pauline families; the Puna community
collective_victims_if_applicable.range_of_impacts: death; decades of wrongful imprisonment; a death in prison; unresolved compensation

characters.name: Ida Smith
characters.role_in_story: Waawaa resident who found Dana alive on the trail
characters.key_actions_they_took: Covered her with a quilt and prayed with her while waiting for a passing motorist; there were no phones in the area (SNIPPET-ONLY) [29][33]

characters.name: John Gonsalves
characters.key_actions_they_took: On May 23, 1994 told authorities Pauline had been present at the attack [26]

characters.name: Michael Ortiz
characters.key_actions_they_took: In May 1999 claimed Ian Schweitzer confessed to him at Hawaii Community Correctional Center; parts of his testimony later found false; the 2025 lawsuit alleges detectives told him what to say (allegation) [13][14][36]

characters.name: Kenneth (Ken) Lawson
characters.key_actions_they_took: Led the fight to free the Schweitzers; worked with Indago and law enforcement on the DNA [5][17][23]
characters.notable_quotes: Called the January 2023 ruling "a long time coming" [17]

characters.name: Judge Peter Kubota
characters.key_actions_they_took: Vacated Ian's conviction January 24, 2023 and Shawn's October 23, 2023 [16][17]
characters.notable_quotes: Said the new DNA evidence "conclusively proves a jury would likely reach a different verdict of acquittal" (SNIPPET-ONLY) [45]

characters.name: Dr. Adam Freeman
characters.key_actions_they_took: Concluded the circular injury was not a human bite mark [14]

characters.name: Stephen Kramer
characters.role_in_story: Former federal prosecutor; Indago Solutions co-founder (with former FBI agent Stephen Busch); credited in reports with the 2018 identification in the Golden State Killer case
characters.key_actions_they_took: Identified Lauro on February 26, 2024 from ancestry, age, genetics and address history; passed the lead to the FBI [2][4][59]
characters.notable_quotes: Paraphrase only: said the DNA match was enough probable cause to arrest, and that the July 19 swab served no purpose other than to tip Lauro off [4]

characters.name: Benjamin Moszkowicz
characters.key_actions_they_took: Announced the identification July 29, 2024; defended not arresting Lauro [1][10][11]
characters.notable_quotes: "The presence of Lauro's DNA at the crime scene was, in and of itself, not sufficient evidence to prove that Lauro intentionally or knowingly caused her death." / "We remain committed, as we have since day one, of solving this case." [11]

characters.name: Kelden Waltjen
characters.notable_quotes: "It is our hope that law enforcement's continued investigation, the advancements in technology that weren't previously available, and the identification of Unknown Male #1 will afford the Ireland family some sense of closure." [11]

characters.name: Albert Lauro Jr.
characters.role_in_story: Man police identified through DNA as 'Unknown Male #1'; 57, of Hawaiian Paradise Park; in his mid-twenties in 1991; reportedly lived in the Kapoho area at the time (SNIPPET-ONLY); no violent criminal history (traffic citations, a civil case with a bank) [1][9]
characters.key_actions_they_took: Voluntarily interviewed July 19, 2024 and gave court-ordered cheek swab; found dead at home July 23, 2024 (apparent suicide); never charged, never tried, never convicted [6][9]

characters.name: Myles Breiner
characters.key_actions_they_took: Pursued posthumous exoneration; hearing delayed January 2024 for lack of an official New Mexico death certificate [23]

characters.name: Daniel Hood
characters.key_actions_they_took: Confessed to killing Pauline with a rock; pleaded to second-degree murder; 15 years [24][25]
characters.notable_quotes: Per New Mexico DPS, said he did it "because he was a snitch and he walked around like he owned the place" [24]

events.what_happened: Shawn meets prosecutors and recants
Judge Peter Kubota vacates Ian's conviction on stipulated new evidence (Unknown Male #1 DNA, bite mark, tire treads, recantation); charges dismissed; Ian released
Shawn's conviction vacated and case dismissed (Deputy Prosecutor Shannon Kagawa agreed)
Pauline's posthumous exoneration hearing delayed: no official death certificate
Indago Solutions identifies Albert Lauro Jr. as the only potential candidate; lead given to FBI
FBI agent and Hawaii police surveil Lauro and collect a fork he discarded in public; it matches Unknown Male #1 (swab from body, hospital sheet, T-shirt)
Lauro voluntarily interviewed; court-ordered cheek swab; asks to leave and is allowed
Lauro, 57, found dead at home; apparent suicide

Schweitzers file federal civil-rights suit (conspiracy, malicious prosecution, due process, emotional distress) against Hawaii County and its police
Trial on state compensation claim set for March 30, 2026
Report: Hawaii Supreme Court asked three questions on whether the brothers can seek state compensation and also sue the county in federal court; both cases on hold; no money received

the_moment.exact_location: Kapoho Kai Drive, Kapoho, Puna, Hawaii Island
the_moment.what_is_happening: A 23-year-old from Virginia rides her sister's bicycle on Christmas Eve
the_moment.what_makes_it_shocking: She was struck, taken miles away, and found alive on a fishing trail; help took more than two hours
the_moment.ironic_twist: The DNA that named a suspect was on her and on a T-shirt from the start; it matched none of the three men sent to prison

cold_open_material.central_mystery_question: If the DNA never matched the three men convicted, whose was it, and why did it take 32 years to find out?

step_by_step_explanation: Crime-scene DNA (rape kit, hospital sheet, T-shirt) yields a single male profile, 'Unknown Male #1', which matched none of the three convicted men and no CODIS offender
Hawaii Innocence Project works with law enforcement and sends samples to Indago Solutions
A dense SNP profile is compared with genealogy databases open to law enforcement to find relatives
Genealogists build family trees from relatives back to a common ancestor and forward to candidates, filtering by ancestry (about 80% Filipino), age and address history
February 26, 2024: one candidate, Albert Lauro Jr.; lead to FBI and Hawaii police
Discarded fork collected under surveillance; match
Court-ordered cheek swab July 19, 2024; confirmation July 24
the_method.why_it_worked: Unlike CODIS, which only matches people already in it, genealogy finds relatives who chose to share their DNA

technical_terms_to_explain.simple_explanation: the FBI's national DNA database of offenders and crime scenes; it only matches people already in it
hundreds of thousands of genetic markers, like a full barcode instead of the 20-point fingerprint used by CODIS
an object a person throws away in public can be collected and tested
a cotton swab rubbed inside the cheek
a legal deadline after which some crimes can no longer be charged; murder has none in Hawaii, sexual assault had expired here

the_method.scale_of_operation: Two companies/agencies (Indago, FBI) plus Hawaii police; identification about five months before confirmation

systemic_failure.institution_that_failed: Hawaii County Police Department and the prosecution of the 1990s; also the emergency response on December 24, 1991
systemic_failure.how_they_were_supposed_to_protect: Find the real attacker and convict on reliable evidence
systemic_failure.why_they_failed: Years of public pressure; reliance on an informant facing his own charges, a jailhouse informant and a teenage co-defendant's plea; DNA exclusions explained away; later-discredited bite-mark testimony
specific_incompetence_examples: Pauline interviewed at least seven times with inconsistent accounts [26]
1998 DNA testing excluded the Schweitzers from the sexual assault, yet they were re-indicted in 1999 on an informant's word [13]
Odontologist who first excluded Ian later testified his teeth were consistent with the mark; defense expert later found it was not a human bite [14]
Tire treads at both scenes did not come from Ian's Volkswagen Beetle [17]
More than two hours before an ambulance reached Dana [29]
systemic_failure.ironic_details_about_the_failure: The evidence that freed the men and named a new suspect was the same evidence collected in 1991

the_investigation.investigating_agency: Hawaii Police Department (Hawaii County), FBI, Hawaii Innocence Project, Indago Solutions
the_investigation.initial_wrong_assumptions: That Pauline's 1994 statements were true and that the unknown DNA could be explained away
the_investigation.the_fatal_mistake: Lauro discarded a fork in public that investigators collected
the_investigation.how_long_until_caught: Identified 32 years and 7 months later; never arrested

the_confrontation.scene_description: Voluntary interview, not in custody; court-ordered buccal swab taken; Lauro asked to leave and was allowed to [6]
the_confrontation.protagonist_reaction: No public account of what he said; police were reviewing the interview transcript and his phone [11]
the_confrontation.ironic_or_absurd_details: He was found dead July 23, one day before the swab confirmed the match [9]

charges_filed: Historic: Pauline (1999), Ian Schweitzer (2000) convicted of murder, kidnapping and sexual assault; Shawn Schweitzer pleaded guilty to manslaughter and kidnapping (2000)
legal_resolution.notable_court_testimony: Sandy Ireland at Pauline's trial; informant Michael Ortiz; forensic odontologist on the bite mark
legal_resolution.sentence_received: Ian: life plus two consecutive 20-year terms (reported as 130 years); Pauline: reports differ (180 years / 160 years / consecutive life terms); Shawn: about one year credited plus five years' probation
legal_resolution.current_status: As of October 2026: Ian and Shawn Schweitzer's convictions vacated and charges dismissed (2023), reportedly without prejudice; they are counted as exonerated by the Innocence Project and the National Registry of Exonerations; county prosecutors have argued a vacated conviction is not proof of innocence and one report says they still call the brothers suspects. Their state compensation claim (HRS 661B, $50,000 per year) and federal civil-rights suit were on hold in September 2026 pending Hawaii Supreme Court questions; no money paid. Pauline died in 2015; a posthumous petition was delayed in January 2024 and no ruling vacating his conviction was found. Albert Lauro Jr. died July 23, 2024, never charged or convicted; police said DNA gave probable cause for sexual assault, whose limitation period had expired, but not enough evidence to charge murder.

details: The DNA that excluded the three men in the 1990s was the same DNA that pointed to a new name in 2024.
Pauline was killed in April 2015, days after the Innocence Project announced the DNA could point to someone else.
Lauro died one day before the confirmatory swab came back.
The sexual assault could no longer be charged because of the statute of limitations; the murder could, but police said they lacked evidence.
The Kapoho road where Dana was struck was buried by lava in 2018.
John Ireland's laws on heinous murders could not be applied retroactively to his own daughter's case.

universal_stakes.why_this_matters_to_viewer: One crime produced two kinds of victims: the young woman killed, and the men convicted for it.
universal_stakes.how_this_could_happen_to_them: Pressure, informants and confident experts can convict anyone.
universal_stakes.lesson_or_warning: Evidence kept and re-tested can correct the system; the truth that comes late is still the truth.
universal_stakes.current_relevance: Genetic genealogy now used both to identify perpetrators and to free the innocent; compensation laws in Hawaii have paid no one as of 2025 reporting.
